(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, at_exit & holding_box & !box_fell) -> u2

(u0, at_exit & holding_box & !box_fell, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, at_exit & holding_box & !box_fell, u2) -> 1.0
feedback: Critical bug: transition (u1, else) -> u0 makes every step in u1 that isn't a terminal holding_box exit drop back to u0. Since box_fell is a one-step event, after one step in u1 the agent is almost always back in u0 via the self-loop-free else edge — worse, while holding the box in u1, the else self-loop is missing, so the (u1) state never persists. The machine should have (u1, else) -> u1 or (u1, box_fell) -> u1 style self-loops so u1 means 'box was picked up / should be carried', and the exit reward in u1 should require holding_box. Also, the stated task is to pick the box up on the very next move after each fall; u1 gives +0.2 on the fall itself rather than rewarding the pickup, and u0's reward never encourages pickup density. Additionally, reward at u1 exit should probably require !box_fell already handled; but the main defect is the broken else from u1 back to u0, which can even wipe out reward tracking mid-episode. Fix: (u1, else) -> u1 with rewards for pickup events; keep terminal u2 as only accepting state.

REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, holding_box, u1) -> 0.2
(u2, holding_box, u1) -> 0.3
(u1, at_exit & holding_box & !box_fell, u5) -> 1.0
feedback: FAIL (semantics/reward). The RM reaches u5 (a FINAL state) only via rewards, which is fine, but the critical flaw is in the reward for box recovery. The task is 'Each time the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.' The transition (u2, holding_box) -> u1 correctly detects picking the box up after a fall, but the reward (u2, holding_box, u1) -> 0.3 is a flat, fixed reward. This does not enforce 'on your very next move': it pays the same reward whether the box is recovered immediately or after 100 steps of wandering. There is no mechanism (e.g., a timeout state or step-counted transition) to penalize delays. Second issue: state u4 is a dead-end non-accepting sink for reaching the exit without the box, but there is no path out of it, and it carries no reward. Because the task says 'If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box' (a hard constraint), failing this should either lead to a terminal fail state with negative reward or keep the episode from being counted as a success, but here it just burns a state. Third: u3 has transition (u3, holding_box) -> u5 but no reward for (u3, holding_box, u5). An agent that reaches the exit first (u0->u3) and then... wait, at_exit ends the episode, so u3 is unreachable in practice, but structurally it is inconsistent: (u3, holding_box) -> u5 exists without a reward entry, while the spec requires a reward for every transition that ends in a FINAL state. Fourth: transitions to u5 exist from u1 and u3, but u5's own self-loop (u5, else) -> u5 has no reward specified, which is acceptable for a sink, but (u3, holding_box, u5) lacking a reward is a spec violation. Fifth: (u1, at_exit & holding_box & !box_fell) -> u5 is correct for the final success, but there's no reward guarding the case where box_fell and at_exit hold together (constraint says they never do, so this is fine). Summary: reject for missing reward on (u3, holding_box, u5), for the dead-end u4 sink without a failure signal, and especially for the u2->u1 reward not enforcing the 'very next move' timing constraint.

Rewards are dense where progress matters (0.1 first pickup, 0.3 re-pickup), bounded, and zero on the pure fall transition. Reachability: every state is reachable and u3 is the only accepting state; if the exit is reached without the box, the machine stays in u1 with no final transition, matching the 0-reward failure.
